title: PackManifest

after.description: Mods it loads after when they run, by alias; they take no version.

breaks.description:
Mods it cannot run beside, by alias; with a `version`, only those
versions.

description.description: One sentence on what it adds.

enshwick.description:
The Enshwick releases it is made for, as a Cargo-style version
requirement such as `=1.0.0-alpha.12` (empty for any); a loader of
another release skips the pack and names both.

exports.description:
What other mods may use, each `<kind>:<local name>` with a kind of
`point`, `event`, `call`, `service`, `content` or `stat`, such as the
events its scripts define: `event:greeted` lets them hear
`<id>:greeted`. The loader refuses them anything else of the pack's.

homepage.description: Where players read about it, an `https://` address.

id.description:
The pack id, `<author>.<name>` like a mod's; it names the folder, the
namespace of the pack's content and its texts override file.

join.description:
Whether server and clients must run the same pack, files and all, to
play together; on unless the pack says otherwise.

name.description: The name players read; the id when empty.

recommends.description: Mods it works with when they run, by alias, loaded first.

replaces.description:
The ids of mods it takes the place of; the loader runs only this
one.

requires.description:
Mods and packs it needs, by the aliases its files and scripts know
them by; the loader runs them first and leaves the pack off without
them.

setting.description:
The pack's settings, in the order the Mods screen shows them; a Luau
mod reads them, as a Rust mod reads its `Config`.

version.description: A Cargo-style version requirement; empty for any.

anyOf.description: The mod's id alone, for any version.
The mod's id with a version requirement.

PackSetting.description:
One setting of a pack, a `[[setting]]` table of `pack.toml`.

# Examples

```
use enshwick::config::Stage;
use enshwick::packs::PackManifest;

let manifest = PackManifest::parse(r#"
id = "you.greeter"
version = "1.0.0"

[[setting]]
key = "greeting"
default = "Welcome"
doc = "What a player who joins reads."

[[setting]]
key = "every"
default = 30
min = 1
stage = "startup"
"#)?;
let schema = manifest.settings_schema().ok_or("no settings")?;
assert_eq!(schema.fields[1].stage, Stage::Startup);
assert_eq!(schema.fields[1].min, Some(1.0));
# Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
```

choices.description: The values it accepts; empty for any.

default.description: The value on first start; its type is the setting's.

doc.description: What it does, for the file's comments and the Mods screen.

key.description: The key in the settings file, of `[a-z0-9_]`.

stage.description: When a change takes effect: `runtime` unless said.

synced.description: A `startup` setting a joined client takes from the server.

text.description:
The key of its translated label in the pack's `texts.toml`;
`config.<key>` unless said.

PackSide.description:
Where a pack runs, in `pack.toml`.

# Examples

See [`PackManifest`].

oneOf.description: The server and the clients: the default, as both read content.

The dedicated server and hosting clients only, such as a pack of
loot alone.

Read when a world loads (or at start, with none); a change takes
effect when the world loads again, and the running values stay until
then.

Applied while the game runs, through the mod's
[`on_config_change`](crate::Load::on_config_change).
Each player's own: never sent to or taken from a server.
The server's value: a joined client runs with it over its own file.

Read once as the game starts, for what only a start can set up, such
as hooks or content: kept in the settings file for every world, and a
change waits for the next start.
